severity: REFRAMES THE STUDY -- per-condition outcomes are not reproducible
claim: For a fixed checkpoint, fixed frozen conditions and deterministic execution, the GRASP stage is perfectly reproducible across processes while the POST-GRASP outcome (lift/carry) is uncorrelated noise.

evidence.protocol: eval_checkpoint.py, deterministic, frozen 25-condition prefix, no frame capture in either run

refutes.previous_hypothesis: g1_piston_render_physics_divergence.json proposed that the renderer's mid-chunk camera reads perturbed contact physics.
refutes.why_refuted: A no-capture rerun in a fresh process reproduces 0 of 5 stored lifts, exactly like the capture-enabled render. Capture is not the cause -- neither run reproduces the other, with or without it.
refutes.status: the capture hypothesis is CLOSED as not-the-cause

implications: Per-condition claims about this task are not supportable. Only aggregate rates are, and only with an uncertainty band that reflects run-to-run variation, not just binomial sampling error.
The matched-condition comparison methodology is undermined: pairing SAC and RLPD on the same condition assumes the condition's outcome is a property of the policy, and post-grasp it is not.
The frozen 25/50-condition suite measures the policy far less precisely than the Wilson intervals suggest, because those intervals assume a fixed per-condition success probability.
Run-to-run variation is a THIRD variance source, alongside training-seed variance and evaluation-condition variance, and it was never budgeted for.
The carry differences that motivated the whole SAC-vs-RLPD comparison (0.36 vs 0.16 vs 0.12) are of the same magnitude as this single-checkpoint run-to-run swing (0.12 -> 0.20).
likely_mechanism: Contact-rich manipulation with a marginal grasp. GPU non-determinism in the VLM forward pass (bf16 autocast, non-deterministic kernels) perturbs the action chunk slightly; PhysX contact resolution amplifies a marginal grasp into a different macroscopic outcome. The chunk-boundary finger snap (see g1_piston_chunk_boundary_jitter.json, 13/22 boundaries above 0.5 rad) plausibly sits right at that margin.
required_next: Repeat-evaluation of a single checkpoint to measure the run-to-run distribution directly, so any reported rate carries an honest interval. Until then no SAC-vs-RLPD ordering, and no per-condition claim, is supportable.

two_distinct_claims.per_condition_outcome_is_noise: SETTLED. Lift and carry condition sets have Jaccard 0.0 across identical-protocol runs, with grasp at Jaccard 1.0 in the same runs as a positive control. Matched per-condition comparison is invalid for lift and carry.
two_distinct_claims.aggregate_rate_is_unreliable: NOT YET ESTABLISHED at n=2 runs. The observed carry spread (0.08) sits INSIDE the Wilson95 width a single run reports (0.28), so a single evaluation is not yet provably over-confident about the RATE. More repeats are needed to bound run-to-run rate variance.

precision_note_2026_08_20.correction: An earlier framing implied the aggregate rates were also shown unreliable. They are not, yet -- only the per-condition outcomes are. The repeat-evaluation run in flight is what decides the rate question.
precision_note_2026_08_20.why_it_still_matters_for_the_study: Even if the rate variance turns out modest, the SAC-vs-RLPD differences in question (0.36 vs 0.16 vs 0.12) are comparable to the already-observed run-to-run rate swing (0.12 -> 0.20 carry), so those comparisons remain under-powered until the noise floor is bounded.

three_run_result_2026_08_20.runs: three identical-protocol deterministic evaluations of rlpd_ckpt_step415140, frozen 25-condition prefix
three_run_result_2026_08_20.run3_detail: 6 lifts, ALL classified as throws -- horizontal displacement 0.0004-0.0115 m against a 0.05 m threshold. The same checkpoint that carried 3 and 5 times in the other two runs carried ZERO times here.
three_run_result_2026_08_20.verdict_now_upgraded: The AGGREGATE RATE is also unreliable, not only the per-condition outcome. A single checkpoint's carry rate spans 0.00-0.20 across identical runs.

study_level_consequence.reading: The spread across ALGORITHMS AND SEEDS (0.24) is barely larger than the spread produced by re-running ONE checkpoint (0.20). Every arm in the study was evaluated exactly once, so the reported carry differences are not distinguishable from evaluation noise.
study_level_consequence.what_survives: Grasp emergence: 0.02 at SFT to ~1.00 after RL, with grasp highly reproducible across eight runs (199/200 attempts, spread 0.040). Not perfectly reproducible -- one run missed one condition entirely, including its reach -- but roughly an order of magnitude more stable than carry.
study_level_consequence.what_does_not: Any carry-level ordering between SAC and RLPD, any per-condition claim, and any 'best checkpoint' selected on carry.
study_level_consequence.four_run_update: With four runs the noise range contains the entire algorithmic range. No carry-based comparison in this study is supportable, including the SAC s1 @414k carry 0.36 that anchored the early narrative.

four_run_result_2026_08_20.threshold_crossed: The run-to-run carry spread (0.360) now EXCEEDS the Wilson95 width a single run reports (0.282). A single evaluation is therefore provably over-confident about the carry rate, not merely suspected of it.
four_run_result_2026_08_20.the_decisive_coincidence: Run 4 of the RLPD checkpoint produced carry 0.36 -- the exact value that made SAC seed 1 look like the strongest arm in the study. The same RLPD checkpoint produced 0.00 two runs earlier.
four_run_result_2026_08_20.containment: The single-checkpoint noise range [0.00, 0.36] now CONTAINS the entire algorithmic range [0.12, 0.36] observed across both algorithms and all seeds.
four_run_result_2026_08_20.spread_is_still_widening: 0.08 at 2 runs, 0.20 at 3, 0.36 at 4 -- the floor estimate has not converged, so 0.36 is a LOWER BOUND on the true noise range.

recommendation.do_not: Resume the three remaining training seeds to completion for a carry-based comparison. That is ~32 GPU-hours to produce three more single-evaluation numbers drawn from a distribution whose spread already covers the entire effect size.
do: Report grasp emergence as the primary result: 0.02 -> ~1.00, perfectly reproducible (spread 0.000, Jaccard 1.0 across five runs).
Report full success as 0.00 for every RL checkpoint in every run, and the SFT stochastic 0.16 as the only success anywhere.
Report the noise floor itself as a methodological contribution, with the power table.
If a carry comparison is still wanted, budget repeats per arm rather than more conditions, and fix the reward exploit first -- 5 of 5 runs show throws, and one run was ALL throws.

FINAL_eight_run_result.protocol: rlpd_ckpt_step415140, frozen 25-condition prefix, deterministic, BLEND_STEPS=0, eight independent processes

correction_at_run_8.what: Grasp was reported as PERFECTLY reproducible (spread 0.000, Jaccard 1.0) through seven runs. The eighth run broke that: grasp 0.96.
correction_at_run_8.the_single_failure: condition 19, where the policy failed even to REACH (reach=False, return -0.65) -- a whole-rollout deviation, not a marginal grasp that slipped.
correction_at_run_8.corrected_claim: Grasp is HIGHLY reproducible (199/200 attempts, spread 0.040, Jaccard 0.99), not perfectly. The dissociation against carry (spread 0.360, Jaccard 0.066) is unchanged and remains the result: grasp is roughly 9x more stable in spread and 15x in per-condition agreement.

FINAL_eight_run_result.lift_also_crossed: At eight runs the LIFT spread (0.360) also exceeds the Wilson95 width a single run reports (0.344), joining carry. Only grasp remains inside its interval.
